name: Gaming and Leisure Properties, Inc.
moat_justification: Long-term triple-net master leases (15-30yr terms, escalators, cross-collateralization, rent coverage >1.8x on most leases, no rent defaults since the 2013 spin-off) and scarce licensed gaming supply give contractual, durable rent — but ROIC proxy has run only ~8.7-10.5% over 2020-2025 (~10.3% in FY2025), there is no pricing power beyond contractual escalators, PENN (34 of 71 properties) and levered Bally's (16 of 71) concentrate tenant credit, and growth is bought with dilutive equity and ~5% debt.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
DILUTION: share count growing 3.3%/yr — already deducted via the growth adjustment; check SBC trend
BASIS_BREAK_SUSPECT: a >60% revenue jump/drop in the last 5 yrs — check for divestitures, big M&A, or restatements before trusting any CAGR

CASH_INCLUDES_RESTRICTED: the only cash tag filed for the latest fiscal year is the combined cash + restricted-cash total and no restricted-cash tag separates it — net debt is UNDERSTATED by the restricted amount (escrow / collateral / regulatory); check the balance sheet before trusting HIGH_NET_DEBT's absence
SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH: Real Estate sector — OE/capex DCF fits real estate names poorly; grade confidence low
HIGH_NET_DEBT: net debt is 6.8x normalized OE — levered OE can vanish fast; stress the bear cases
TIER_BAND: bear-case tier C (10.2%) vs bull-case tier B (15.2%) — the verdict spans tiers; size any position to the bear end
one_liner: Durable triple-net gaming landlord, moat 5/10 — contractual rent and no defaults since 2013, but at $39.28 it does not clear 15% (weighted IRR 12.9%, IV@15% $32.65); it clears 15% only at ~$32.65, and the OE/capex model fits REITs poorly (sector misfit, confidence low).
moat_for: Triple-net master leases: 15-30yr terms, annual escalators, cross-collateralization and corporate guarantees; tenants pay taxes, insurance and maintenance
No rent defaults since inception (2013 spin-off); most leases carry rent coverage above 1.8x
Scarce, license-limited gaming real estate in 21 states — tenants cannot readily relocate a casino
ROIC proxy stable at ~9-10.5% through the 2020 COVID year and the rate shock (10.3% FY2025)
moat_against: Tenant concentration: PENN operates 34 of 71 properties and levered Bally's 16 of 71 — tenant credit is the moat's weak leg
No pricing power beyond contractual escalators; rent growth is capped by lease terms
Single-sector portfolio (gaming only) exposed to regional-casino consumer and regulatory risk
Growth requires external capital: share count +3.3%/yr and net debt 6.8x normalized OE at ~5% average cost
ROIC proxy only ~10% — a modest spread over the cost of capital for a levered REIT
